'''Yarna d'al' Gargan''' was a [[Gender|female]] [[Askajian]] whose [[Parent|father]] was a tribal [[chief]] back on her [[homeworld]] of [[Askaji]]. She was captured by [[enslaver]]s and transported to the [[desert]] [[planet]] of [[Tatooine]], where the [[Hutt]] [[crime lord]] [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure]] bought her. As an [[Slavery|enslaved]] being, she was forced to serve him as a dancing girl at [[Boba Fett's Palace|his palace]]. While working alongside a young [[Twi'lek]] called [[Oola]], she was present for Oola's execution and the arrival of [[Luke Skywalker]] at the palace. She escaped after Jabba's [[death]] and recovered her kidnapped [[Youngling|cublings]] from his [[Desilijic Complex|townhouse]].

==Biography==
===Enslavement===
Yarna d'al' Gargan was an [[Askajian]] [[Gender|female]] with [[Color|dark brown]] [[hair]] who came from [[Askaji]],<ref name="Character Encyclopedia" /> a [[planet]] in the [[Outer Rim Territories]].<ref name="SW:TFA Beginner Game">[[Star Wars: The Force Awakens Beginner Game|''Star Wars: The Force Awakens'' Beginner Game]]</ref> Her people lived in tribes led by chiefs, one of whom was her [[Yarna d'al' Gargan's parent|parent]],<ref name="Alien Archive">''[[Star Wars: Alien Archive]]''</ref> and she would dance for the honor of her tribe. She was [[Marriage|married]] to [[Nautag]] and the mother of four [[Youngling|cublings]]. One [[Standard day|day]], however, she and her family were captured by [[enslaver]]s and brought to the [[desert]] planet [[Tatooine]], where the [[Hutt]] [[crime lord]] [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure]] bought them. When Nautag attempted to rebel, the Hutt fed him to his pet [[rancor]],<ref name="Character Encyclopedia" /> [[Pateesa]],<ref name="Aftermath: Life Debt">''[[Aftermath: Life Debt]]''</ref> and Yarna's cublings were sent to Jabba's [[Desilijic Complex|townhouse]] in [[Mos Eisley]].<ref name="Character Encyclopedia" />

[[File:FlirtyGargan-ROTJ.png|thumb|right|300px|Yarna d'al' Gargan was a slave of Jabba Desilijic Tiure.]]
Jabba kept numerous [[Slavery|enslaved]] dancers<ref name="Visual Encyclopedia">''[[Star Wars: The Visual Encyclopedia]]''</ref> at [[Boba Fett's Palace|his palace]] in the [[Dune Sea]]. Yarna became one of the dancing girls,<ref name="DB Yarna" /> and although she hated the Hutt, she became close to some of his palace regulars<ref name="Character Encyclopedia" /> and knew how to avoid Jabba's temper. Considering her to be his favorite performer,<ref name="Absolutely Everything">''[[Star Wars: Absolutely Everything You Need to Know]]''</ref> one of Jabba's whims was forcing her to wear makeup to look more like [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure's mother|his mother]], and her increased size was meant to resemble a Hutt's. Her slow and deliberate dances contrasted with those of the young [[Twi'lek]] [[Oola]],<ref name="DB Yarna" /> with whom she often performed duets in front of Jabba's [[throne]].<ref name="Geektionary">''[[Star Wars: Geektionary: The Galaxy from A - Z]]''</ref> She remained Jabba's dancer for many years.<ref name="Character Encyclopedia" />

===Last dance with Oola===
In [[4 ABY]],<ref name="Date">''[[Star Wars: Galactic Atlas]]'' dates the events of {{Film|VI}} to [[4 ABY]].</ref> Gargan was stood with a drink, chatting to another courtier in one of the booths of Jabba's throne room when Jabba's [[majordomo]], [[Bib Fortuna]], and a pair of [[Gamorrean]] guards escorted the [[droid]]s [[C-3PO]] and [[R2-D2]] into the room. R2-D2 then played a [[Hologram|holographic]] message to Jabba from the [[Jedi]] [[Luke Skywalker]], the master of the two droids. In the message, the Jedi asked to bargain with Jabba for the freedom of the Hutt's prisoner [[Han Solo]], a friend of Skywalker's who Jabba kept frozen in [[carbonite]]. After the message ended with Skywalker gifting the droids to Jabba, the Hutt declared he had no interest in negotiating over Solo, and the droids were taken away.<ref name="ROTJ" />

[[File:OolaGargan-Dancing-ROTJ.png|thumb|left|300px|Yarna d'al' Gargan often danced with Oola.]]
After the droids had been set to work, the [[Max Rebo Band]] performed the [[Music|song]] "[[Jedi Rocks]] for Jabba, and Gargan and Oola danced in the center of the throne room before Jabba's throne during the performance. When the song ended, Jabba demanded it be played again, and the band obliged with the Askajian and the Twi'lek both continuing to dance. During the second performance, Jabba attempted to pull Oola closer to him while Gargan kept dancing, but when the Twi'lek resisted, Jabba interrupted the song by dropping her through a trap door into a pit beneath the throne room. Having stopped dancing, Gargan then joined other courtiers in gathering around a grating in the throne room floor to<ref name="ROTJ" /> helplessly<ref name="Geektionary" /> watch as the screaming Oola was devored by Pateesa. The Askajian clutched her belly while laughing at her fellow dancer's fate as others present cheered.<ref name="ROTJ" />

===A princess in disguise===
[[File:Gargan-Laughing-ROTJ.png|thumb|right|300px|Yarna d'al' Gargan laughed at Oola's fate.]]
As the commotion died down after Oola's death, the courts attention was drawn to the throne room's entry way by the sound of [[blaster]] fire. The source of the noise was revealed to be [[Princess]] [[Leia Skywalker Organa Solo|Leia Organa]], who entered the throne room disguised as the [[bounty hunter]] [[Boushh]] and dragged the [[Wookiee]] [[Chewbacca]] before Jabba's throne where Gargan had previously been dancing. Organa demanded double the [[bounty]] Jabba had placed on the Wookiee and threatened the room with an active [[thermal detonator]], causing the court to cower in terror. Jabba merely laughed and gave an increased, but not doubled, counter offer, which satisfied the disguised Organa. With the detonator deactivated, Chewbacca was taken away and the band began playing music again.<ref name="ROTJ" />

Later that [[Standard day|night]], Gargan was [[sleep]]ing beside the [[Quarren]] [[Tessek]] in one of the booths of the throne room when Organa snuck back. She passed the sleeping dancer in order to reach her true objective in the palace: the [[smuggler]] [[Han Solo]], who was frozen in [[carbonite]] and displayed on Jabba's wall. After she freed Solo, Jabba, who had been lying in wait with many other members of his court, sprung a trap on Organa and captured both her and Solo.<ref name="ROTJ" /> After the pair's capture, the court celebrated late into the night.<ref name="Darkside">''[[Return of the Jedi: Beware the Power of the Dark Side!]]''</ref>

===Freedom at last===
[[File:GarganTessek-ROTJ.png|thumb|left|300px|Yarna d'al' Gargan was close with some members of Jabba's court.]]
The next morning,<ref name="Darkside" /> Jabba and his court were dozing after their late night. Gargan was resting again in one of the throne room booths with her head on Tessek's shoulder when the [[Jedi Knight]] [[Luke Skywalker]] arrived in the throne room. Gargan awoke just before Jabba's [[majordomo]], [[Bib Fortuna]], having been [[mind trick]]ed by the [[Jedi]], woke the Hutt as the Jedi demanded that Jabba free Solo and Chewbacca. Gargan and Tessek stood together among other court members as Jabba refused Skywalker's demands, prompting the Jedi to threaten the Hutt with a [[DL-18 blaster pistol|blaster pistol]]. The Hutt then dropped Skywalker, and the unlucky [[Gamorrean]] guard [[Jubnuk]], into the rancor pit.<ref name="ROTJ" />

Once again the court gather round to watch the execution, but instead of perishing like Oola had, Skywalker killed the rancor after it devored Jubnuk. Outraged, Jabba demanded that Skywalker, Solo, and Chewbacca be brought before him. Still stood with Tessek, Gargan watched as the Hutt sentenced all three to be executed at the [[Great Pit of Carkoon]] and then the pair joined the crowd of courtiers that followed the [[prisoner]]s as they were marched from the throne room. Jabba and much of his court then traveled to the Great Pit of Carkoon aboard the [[sail barge]] ''[[Khetanna]]'', but at the pit Skywalker and his allies fought back against their captors. Organa ultimately killed the Hutt before destroying the sail barge, killing many of Jabba's followers.<ref name="ROTJ" /> Thanks to Organa's actions, Yarna escaped Jabba's palace and was reunited with her cublings.<ref name="Character Encyclopedia" />

==Personality and traits==
Due to Jabba's demands of her appearance,<ref name="Character Encyclopedia" /> the 1.5 [[meter]] tall Gargan had an ample figure<ref name="DB Yarna" /> with a generous six-[[breast]]ed chest.<ref name="Geektionary" /> As well as being more slow and deliberate in her dancing than Oola,<ref name="DB Yarna" /> the Askajian improvised her performances to be more humerous than the Twi'lek's graceful and dainty choreography.<ref name="Geektionary" />

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:Gargan-ConceptArt.png|thumb|right|300px|Concept art of Yarna d'al' Gargan]]
Yarna d'al' Gargan was portrayed by [[Claire Davenport]] in the [[1983]] [[original trilogy]] film, [[Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi|''Star Wars'': Episode VI ''Return of the Jedi'']].<ref name="ROTJ" /> Director [[Richard Marquand]] cast her after having directed her in [[Wikipedia:Birth of the Beatles|''Birth of the Beatles'']], a [[1979]] biopic about [[Wikipedia:The Beatles|The Beatles]], in which Davenport played a nude model. Marquand said, "I selected the fat lady, because I think fat ladies are wonderful." He originally envisioned the character as a daughter to Jabba the Hutt.<ref name="Making">''[[The Making of Return of the Jedi]]''</ref>

Concept art of the character was created in [[1981]].<ref name="Chronicles">''[[Star Wars Chronicles]]''</ref> [[Nilo Rodis-Jamero]], costume designer of ''Return of the Jedi'', said that Yarna d'al' Gargan's six breasts were decided upon in a conversation while under the influence of alcohol. Her costume used a [[Wikipedia:Foam latex|foam latex]] [[Wikipedia:Prosthetic makeup|prosthetic]] on her stomach,<ref name="Insider 158">{{InsiderCite|158|Star Wars Style Part 6: Return of the Jedi|''Star Wars'' Style Part 6: ''Return of the Jedi''}}</ref> which was fabricated by [[Industrial Light & Magic]] and shipped to London for filming.<ref name="Wiebba-Wiebba" />

The character was not named Yarna d'al' Gargan during the production of ''Return of the Jedi''. In [[2006]], [[Holocron continuity database]] keeper [[Leland Chee]] identified a production name "[[Weeba Weeba]]" as assigned to a human rancor keeper.<ref name="Holocron">{{Blog|holocron|27/comments|Jabba's Skiff Guards}}</ref> However, research by [[Pablo Hidalgo]] for a [[StarWars.com]] blog post in [[2013]] uncovered that during production of ''Return of the Jedi'', Davenport's character was known as Wiebba-Wiebba.<ref name="Wiebba-Wiebba">{{SW|url=news/star-wars-mysteries-who-is-wiebba-wiebba|series=Star Wars Mysteries|text=Who is Wiebba-Wiebba?}}</ref>

After the film, [[Kenner Products]] began designing an action figure of Gargan for the toy line [[Star Wars: The Power of the Force (1985 toy line)|''Star Wars: The Power of the Force'']]. [[Lucasfilm]] put a stop to production in its intermediate prototype stage, apparently considering the six-breasted dancer inappropriate for a children's toy.<ref name="Insider 92">{{InsiderCite|92|The Toys That Never Were}}</ref> Her first action figure was released in [[2008]] as part of [[Hasbro]]'s ''[[Star Wars: The Legacy Collection]]''.<ref name="Hasbro">{{HasbroCite|set=Star Wars: The Legacy Collection|pack=#06: Yarna d'al' Gargan|altlink=https://www.rebelscum.com/TLC06Yarna.asp}}</ref>

The [[2021]] poetic adaptation of ''Return of the Jedi'', ''[[The Odyssey of Star Wars: An Epic Poem]]'', by [[Jack Mitchell]] describes Gargan as leading a dance while the Max Rebo Band plays when Luke Skywalker arrives at the palace, rather than sleeping, as is depicted in the film.<ref name="Odyssey">''[[The Odyssey of Star Wars: An Epic Poem]]''</ref>
